plants.name: Wisteria floribunda
plants.description: Long, fragrant chains of pea-like flowers hang from twisting woody vines. In famous Japanese gardens they form glowing tunnels and ceilings of cascading blossom. Bees visit the blooms constantly.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late April to mid-May in Japan, so April 30 falls within the season.
plants.location: Japan, especially the wisteria gardens of Honshu
plants.funFact: Wisteria vines twine in a set direction. Japanese wisteria twists clockwise, while Chinese wisteria twists counterclockwise. Old vines can live for well over a century and grow thick enough to support their own weight like tree trunks.
